top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) is the most reproducible and cleanly attributed result on the slate: Katori's magic-wavelength condition lets thousands of neutral atoms be trapped and interrogated in parallel without first-order light-shift perturbation, removing the single-ion statistics limit, and the 10^-18 systematics (blackbody, lattice light, collisions, density) have been identified and verified by direct clock-to-clock comparisons across continents. It is a new experimental regime, distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-system control prizes, with a compact two-laureate allocation and a citation limited to the lattice clock. P001 (magic-angle graphene) is a genuine new platform but is under a decade old, has an unsettled mechanism and an unresolved attribution gap (Cao and earlier band-structure work are outside the three names), so it ranks second; a prize this year is still preferable to none.
recusal_note: No direct conflict apparent from profile; mild distant connection only in that I spent a year in John Hall's lab during my PhD, and Hall's 2005 prize is part of the lineage discussed, but I have no apparent link to Katori or Ye.
